$schema_note: Machine-readable re-verification of the SoulSystem static audit. Every finding was re-read against the current source at reverified_against_main; statuses are not inherited from the previous register or from SECURITY_INVARIANTS.md. Paths are repository-relative. Line numbers are deliberately omitted from evidence fields because they go stale; evidence cites files and symbols instead.
method: Static re-verification against current main: each finding's cited code was re-read in the working tree; reachability was established from the soulsystem binary entry points (src/main.rs, src/lib.rs module declarations) and by workspace-wide ripgrep inventories cross-referenced with cargo metadata package roots, excluding the untracked-by-workspace os-agents/ and soullink-node/ duplicate trees. Cited regression tests were confirmed to exist by symbol search and executed for every FIXED_AND_VERIFIED finding. Findings marked REQUIRES_RUNTIME_VERIFICATION need dynamic confirmation that static reading cannot supply.

status_legend.CONFIRMED_CURRENT: Defective behaviour still exists and is reachable; carries reachable_from and reproducer.
status_legend.PARTIALLY_FIXED: A meaningful correction landed but the full invariant is not held; carries remaining_exposure and follow_up.
status_legend.FIXED_AND_VERIFIED: Root cause removed on the production-reachable path and proven by a current in-tree test; carries fixing_prs and verification_tests.
status_legend.NOT_REACHABLE: Defective code still exists but no supported production entry point reaches it; carries unreachable_because.
status_legend.FALSE_POSITIVE: The original claim was factually incorrect.
status_legend.REQUIRES_RUNTIME_VERIFICATION: Static inspection cannot decide; the required dynamic test is stated.
status_legend.DEFERRED_PRODUCT_DECISION: Remaining work needs an explicit product/governance decision; carries decision_required.

findings.title: Unsandboxed Tool Dispatch in Live Agent Path
original_reachable_path: AutonomousAgent::run_react -> async_dispatch_tool -> dispatch_tool -> execute_shell -> bare std::process::Command
findings.current_state: The original vector is closed: soul_tools::execute_shell constructs a soul_sandbox::Sandbox and no bare Command remains on the agent tool-dispatch path. Re-examined more precisely at this commit, correcting an overstatement in the previous re-verification: of the three process-execution sites in src/self_healer.rs, only ONE was ever live. `read_system_stats` ran `df --output=pcent` on every tick of the 30-second run() loop spawned from src/main.rs. The KillNonEssential and RestartService arms exec `kill` and `systemctl`, but no producer in the workspace constructs either DefenseAction variant - Preservation emits only Throttle, MemoryDump, EmergencySave, LocalFallback, DistressSignal and GracefulShutdown - so those two arms were latent, not attacker-reachable as previously described. Both classes are now addressed: the df exec is replaced by a statvfs(3) call (SelfHealer::root_disk_used_percent), removing the spawn entirely rather than sandboxing it; `kill(1)` is replaced by a direct libc::kill signal; and both privileged arms are gated behind ProcessControl::Enabled, which defaults to Disabled, so adding a producer cannot by itself turn bus traffic into host process control. The systemctl unit name is additionally validated by is_safe_service_name. tests/architecture_process_execution.rs now pins the permitted set of process-spawning files in the soulsystem binary crate and fails CI on any new one.
findings.remaining_exposure: The architecture guard covers the root soulsystem binary crate (src/) only. The wider workspace inventory - 110 process-execution matches across 25 workspace-member crates, including 22 in the separate soul-kernel binary - is not yet enforced; each would need classifying before the guard could be widened without false positives. soul-automodify still invokes `cargo` and the soul_gateway iMessage provider still invokes `osascript`, both outside the sandbox and outside this guard's scope. RestartService, when explicitly enabled, still spawns systemctl unsandboxed by design - restarting a host unit is inherently a host operation, so the control is that it is opt-in, not that it is confined.
findings.required_invariant: No production-reachable code path invokes process execution outside the approved soul_sandbox executor (INV-EXEC-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR D-1): route the agent execution path through the sandbox (CRIT-001)

findings.residual_risk: Agent tool dispatch is sandboxed and tested, the binary's only live unsandboxed spawn is gone, and new ones in src/ now fail CI. Workspace-wide enforcement, and the soul-automodify / iMessage spawns, remain open.
findings.follow_up: Classify the 110 workspace-wide process-execution matches and widen tests/architecture_process_execution.rs beyond src/; route soul-automodify's cargo invocation and the soul_gateway iMessage osascript invocation through soul_sandbox or gate them.

findings.title: Unknown Tool Fallthrough Creates Arbitrary Executable Dispatch
original_reachable_path: AutonomousAgent::run_react -> async_dispatch_tool -> dispatch_tool wildcard `_ =>` -> execute_shell
findings.current_state: dispatch_tool_in resolves the name through ToolId::from_name before any handler is selected; from_name matches the six registered identifiers byte-for-byte (no trimming, case-folding or Unicode normalisation) and returns ToolError::UnknownTool otherwise. The remaining `_ =>` arm in async_dispatch_tool sits AFTER from_name has already succeeded, so it is a wildcard over the validated ToolId enum, not over caller-supplied strings; it delegates to dispatch_tool, which re-validates. There is no path from an unregistered name to process execution.
findings.required_invariant: An unregistered tool name can only produce UnknownTool; it can never reach process execution (INV-TOOL-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR B): reject unknown tools via a typed registry (fixes CRIT-002)

findings.residual_risk: Registered process tools still depend on the sandbox guarantees tracked under CRIT-001/HIGH-003. Adding a new ToolId variant that maps to execution remains a code-review concern rather than a test-enforced one.

findings.title: Incorrect Capability Classification for File Tools (write_file/patch_file default to Read/safe and auto-approve)
original_reachable_path: tool capability derived from caller-supplied metadata; write_file/patch_file classified ReadOnly
findings.current_state: ToolId::capability is a total match on the trusted enum: ExecuteShell -> ProcessExecution, ReadFile -> ReadOnly, WriteFile | PatchFile -> FileWrite, BrowserRead -> NetworkRead, McpCall -> NetworkWrite. It takes no caller input, so a request cannot downgrade a capability.
findings.required_invariant: Every tool has a trusted, statically-registered capability the caller cannot downgrade (INV-TOOL-2).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR C): typed capabilities + central classification (fixes CRIT-003)

findings.residual_risk: Capability is correctly assigned, but enforcement breadth (which capabilities a given caller may exercise) is a policy-engine concern; not every consumer consults it.

findings.title: Arbitrary Filesystem Writes Without Path Restrictions
original_reachable_path: write_file/patch_file tool -> std::fs::write with caller-controlled absolute path
findings.current_state: FsPolicy::new canonicalises the declared root; resolve_read/resolve_write canonicalise the nearest existing ancestor of the requested path and reject anything that escapes the root, which closes both `..` traversal and symlink escape (including a symlinked directory ancestor). Writes go through atomic_write (temp + rename).
findings.required_invariant: File tools cannot write outside their declared canonical root; symlink escape and check-then-open races are prevented (INV-FS-1/2/4).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR E): canonical filesystem roots + atomic writes (fixes CRIT-004)

findings.residual_risk: Protection covers the soul_tools file tools only. Other crates writing durable state (soul-memory, journals, skills) do not all route through FsPolicy. Config/secret path protection beyond .git remains deployment-specific (INV-FS-3 PARTIAL).

findings.title: Tool Output Persisted to CCOS Causal Memory & Planner History Before Injection Screening
original_reachable_path: run_react -> raw tool output -> CCOS causal memory + planner ActionHistory before any injection screening
findings.current_state: Persistence entry points take &screening::ScreenedContent rather than &str, so the type system prevents calling them with unscreened output. run_react screens first via screen_tool_output and passes the screened value; content classified Malicious is quarantined with the raw payload withheld.
findings.required_invariant: Tool output is screened before it can be persisted to causal memory or planner history; quarantined content never re-enters prompts (INV-MEM-1/2).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR H): screen tool output before persisting to CCOS/planner (CRIT-005)

findings.residual_risk: Screening is heuristic, so novel injection phrasings may be classified Safe. Enforcement is by type at the soul-agent-core persistence sites; other crates that write to the same stores directly are not type-constrained (see INV-MEM-3, provenance/trust metadata still absent).

findings.title: Unauthenticated State-Changing Gateway/API Routes (auth middleware still absent; production now fail-closed by startup guard)
original_reachable_path: axum router -> state-changing /v1 handlers with no authentication middleware
findings.current_state: soul_gateway::router applies require_auth as a route_layer over every /v1/* operator route, comparing the bearer token with constant_time_eq and failing closed when unconfigured. /health is intentionally unauthenticated. The ws_bridge half is now also fail-closed: WsBridgeConfig gained UnauthenticatedAccess (default Deny), so with no usable shared secret handle_connection refuses the connection before the WebSocket handshake instead of initialising `authenticated = true` as it previously did; a blank or whitespace-only secret is treated as unset by effective_secret() so a misconfigured empty value cannot become a credential; and the token comparison now uses a constant-time equality rather than `token == secret`, closing a timing side channel that the gateway had already closed for its bearer token. src/prod_guard.rs no longer hardcodes the bridge's posture: assemble_posture receives the real WsBridgeConfig and reports authenticated exactly when a usable secret is configured, so production startup aborts with an UnauthenticatedListener violation while the bridge is unauthenticated. Serving without authentication now requires the operator to set SOULSYSTEM_WS_BRIDGE_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED, and that opt-in is deliberately NOT reported as authentication.
findings.remaining_exposure: src/api.rs still builds a Router with no authentication layer, served on 127.0.0.1:9023; it is reported to the guard as unauthenticated (so production startup fails on it too) but has no auth of its own and is mitigated only by the loopback bind. Distinct per-scope authorization is still not implemented anywhere: every authenticated caller has full operator power. The three /providers/*/webhook routes carry no bearer auth by design and rely on the fail-closed secret check tracked under HIGH-007, whose signature verification remains outstanding.
findings.required_invariant: Every state-changing endpoint requires authentication and an authorization scope (INV-NET-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR F): mandatory gateway authentication + webhook fail-closed (CRIT-007)
Integrate platforms, automations, and secure remote runtime

findings.residual_risk: The gateway and the ws bridge both fail closed and are covered by tests; src/api.rs and per-scope authorization are not. The bridge's loopback default bind remains a compensating control, not a proven one.
findings.follow_up: Add authentication to src/api.rs or move its routes behind the gateway; implement distinct per-scope authorization so an operator token is not all-or-nothing.

findings.title: Secrets Never Zeroized (SecretsCrypto master_key is plain Vec<u8>)
original_reachable_path: SecretsCrypto::master_key held as a plain Vec<u8>, never zeroized on drop
findings.current_state: master_key is a secrecy::Secret (zeroized on drop) and derive_key returns Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, so derived key material is wiped as well.
findings.required_invariant: Secrets use redacting/zeroizing types; Debug/Display never reveal them (INV-SEC-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR J): zeroize secret key material in soullink-secrets (fixes HIGH-001)

findings.residual_risk: Only soullink-secrets is converted. Gateway and LLM provider structs still hold tokens/secrets in ordinary String fields, so INV-SEC-1 remains PARTIAL workspace-wide; a full sweep is outstanding.

findings.title: Unreachable Security Components Create False Security Posture
original_reachable_path: security components (validators, seccomp, TLS config) existed but had no production call site, creating a false security posture
findings.current_state: Several previously-dead components are now genuinely wired: StructuralValidator is invoked from the skill crystallization path (PR #85), seccomp::install_filter is invoked from the sandbox pre_exec and is mandatory by default (PR #84), and TlsConfig is now reachable through serve_with_tls (PR #93). The general problem is not eliminated: the process-execution inventory shows 110 matches across 25 workspace crates with no architecture test tying them to the approved executor, and there is still no CI guard that fails when a security component loses its last caller.
findings.remaining_exposure: No automated reachability guard exists, so a future refactor can silently orphan a security component again, exactly as happened originally.
findings.required_invariant: Security components claimed by documentation must have a production call site proven by a test.

fixing_prs.title: security(PR D-2): fail-closed seccomp + network namespace isolation
security(PR K): mandatory validation gate for skill crystallization (fixes HIGH-004)
Integrate platforms, automations, and secure remote runtime

findings.residual_risk: Verification is per-component and manual; the class of defect (silently unreachable security code) has no systemic guard.
findings.follow_up: Add a CI reachability/architecture test asserting each named security component has a non-test caller.

findings.title: soul_sandbox provides string-filtering + optional seccomp only, not OS-level isolation; reachable with no-seccomp default policy
original_reachable_path: soul_sandbox applied string filtering and an optional seccomp profile only; no OS-level isolation
findings.current_state: Real OS-level controls now exist. seccomp is on by default (SandboxPolicy::default().seccomp_profile is Some("default")) and fails closed: install_filter errors propagate out of pre_exec and abort the fork before exec. PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS is set unconditionally first, so the filter installs for unprivileged callers, not only root. Output is bounded by max_output_bytes (2 MiB default) via read_capped, and the process group is killed on timeout. Network isolation via unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET) is deliberately best-effort: on hosts where AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces (Ubuntu 23.10+, GitHub Actions runners) it logs and continues rather than blocking all execution.
findings.remaining_exposure: No cgroup limits: CPU, memory, pids and file-descriptor counts are unbounded, so a sandboxed process can still exhaust host resources. Mount and PID namespaces are not applied, so the filesystem view and process table are shared. Network isolation is not guaranteed - on a restricted host the command runs with full host network access.
findings.required_invariant: Process tools run under OS-level isolation with bounded resources and no network by default (INV-EXEC-2/3/4).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR D-2): fail-closed seccomp + network namespace isolation

findings.residual_risk: Resource exhaustion is unmitigated. Network isolation silently degrades, which is the documented and intended trade-off but still means egress cannot be relied upon as a control.
findings.follow_up: Implement cgroup v2 CPU/memory/pids/fd limits and mount/PID namespaces; add per-tool egress allowlisting instead of all-or-nothing network isolation.

findings.title: Self-Modification (skill crystallization) Without Mandatory Validation Gate
original_reachable_path: crystallize_skills -> SkillLoader::save_skill with an unvalidated, caller-derived skill name -> path traversal
findings.current_state: is_safe_skill_name classifies the name via Path::components, accepting only a single Normal component and additionally rejecting backslashes; SkillLoader::save_skill enforces it before writing and StructuralValidator::validate enforces the same check, so the crystallization path cannot write outside the skills directory.
findings.required_invariant: Skill crystallization validates structure and name safety before persisting (INV-MOD-3).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR K): mandatory validation gate for skill crystallization (fixes HIGH-004)

findings.residual_risk: Validation is structural and name-based; it does not semantically assess skill body content for dangerous instructions.

findings.title: CCOS Memory Uses Non-Atomic Persistence
original_reachable_path: CCOS write_json / KernelSnapshot::save -> std::fs::write (truncate-in-place, torn write on crash)
findings.current_state: Both CCOS persistence entry points now call util::write_durable, which writes to a temporary file, fsyncs, and renames over the target.
findings.required_invariant: CCOS and other durable stores use atomic writes (INV-PERSIST-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR L): route CCOS persistence.rs/persist.rs through atomic write_durable

findings.residual_risk: Each file is individually atomic, but multi-file consistency is not transactional: a crash between two related writes can still leave the three CCOS files mutually inconsistent. Corruption detection on load and state versioning are absent (INV-PERSIST-1 remains PARTIAL for that reason).

findings.title: SoulEntity Simulated Autonomy
original_reachable_path: --entity CLI flag -> SoulEntity autonomous loop reporting simulated plan execution
findings.current_state: soul_entity/src/entity.rs still reports plan execution with the literal feedback string "Plan execute avec succes (simulation)" rather than performing or verifying real execution, and the autonomous loop advances on a tokio::time::sleep tick. src/main.rs declares an `entity` CLI flag documented as 'Start the unified autonomous entity (SoulEntity + gateway + skills)' and imports SoulEntity, so the path is reachable in a supported build.
reachable_from: src/main.rs --entity flag -> SoulEntity -> autonomous_loop -> simulated plan feedback
findings.reproducer: Inspect soul_entity/src/entity.rs: the success feedback string is a compile-time constant containing '(simulation)' and is not derived from any executor result. Run the binary with --entity and observe plans reported successful without a corresponding tool invocation.
findings.required_invariant: Placeholder/simulated features never return a successful status in production (INV-TRUTH-1).
findings.residual_risk: An operator using --entity receives success reports for work that was never executed, which can mask failures and corrupt any downstream learning signal that consumes the outcome.
findings.follow_up: Either wire SoulEntity plan execution to the real executor, or gate --entity behind an experimental feature flag and have it report a non-success status.

findings.title: Webhook Verifications Lenient When Secrets Unset
original_reachable_path: POST /providers/*/webhook accepted unsigned payloads when the provider secret was unset
findings.current_state: Both halves are now closed. The handlers still fail closed when a provider secret is unset (PR F), and a configured deployment now cryptographically verifies the request. The handlers previously used axum's Json(payload) extractor, which consumes the body - signature verification requires the raw bytes, so they now take HeaderMap + Bytes, verify, and only then deserialize via parse_verified_body. Per provider, verified against the actual scheme rather than the roadmap's shorthand: Discord uses Ed25519 (NOT HMAC) over `timestamp || body` with DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY as a hex public key; Slack uses HMAC-SHA256 over the base string `v0:{timestamp}:{body}`; Meta/WhatsApp uses HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body via X-Hub-Signature-256. HMAC comparisons use subtle::ConstantTimeEq; Ed25519 verification is constant-time by construction. Timestamp freshness is enforced within MAX_SKEW (5 minutes, both directions) for Discord and Slack; Meta sends no timestamp, so replay protection carries that weight alone for WhatsApp. A ReplayCache on GatewayState rejects any signature already accepted, evicting entries older than MAX_SKEW so it stays bounded. Every rejection reason returns one opaque 401 and is logged server-side only, so a caller cannot distinguish a bad signature from a stale timestamp and probe the difference.
findings.required_invariant: Webhooks fail closed when a secret is unset and reject invalid/replayed signatures (INV-NET-3).

fixing_prs.title: security(P1-1): verify webhook signatures, freshness and replay (commit SHA; merge SHA differs)

findings.residual_risk: Verification is unit-tested against signatures generated with the real algorithms, including genuine Ed25519 signing, rather than mocks. It has not been exercised against live traffic from the three providers, so a header-name or encoding mismatch would only surface in a real integration. The replay cache is per-process and in-memory: a multi-instance deployment behind a load balancer would not share it, so a captured request could be replayed once per instance within the freshness window.

findings.title: Runtime Fragmentation: three parallel agent runtimes, duplicate Telegram bots and sandboxes, and a dead sandboxed AsyncShellExecutor bypassed by an unsandboxed shell path
original_reachable_path: src/main.rs dispatches to AutonomousAgent (--daemon) and SoulEntity (--entity); soul-kernel is a separate binary with its own LLM/memory/state
findings.current_state: The narrow, low-risk sub-issue is fixed: PR #88 removed the dead AutonomousAgent::executor field, an AsyncShellExecutor constructed but never referenced, which falsely implied a second sandboxing mechanism. The broad claim is unchanged. src/main.rs still dispatches to AutonomousAgent and SoulEntity as separate runtimes with separate memory and sandbox abstractions, soul-kernel remains an independent [[bin]] with 22 of its own process-execution call sites, and both clawd::run_bot and the soul_gateway Telegram provider can poll the same bot token.
findings.decision_required: Product/architecture owners must decide which agent runtime is canonical, whether --entity and the standalone soul-kernel binary remain supported, and whether the duplicate Telegram polling path is removed. Consolidation changes user-visible behaviour and cannot be chosen unilaterally by an engineering pass.
findings.required_invariant: Exactly one agent runtime abstraction is reachable from the soulsystem binary's entry points (INV-EXEC-5).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR N): remove dead AutonomousAgent::executor field

findings.residual_risk: Each additional runtime carries an independent security posture; a control proven for AutonomousAgent (sandboxed dispatch, budgets, emergency stop) is not automatically true for SoulEntity or soul-kernel.
findings.follow_up: Product decision on the canonical runtime, then a consolidation PR that removes or explicitly experimental-gates the others.

findings.title: Planner ActionHistory records every tool call as success=true, ignoring tool_ok
original_reachable_path: run_react tool loop -> ActionHistory::record(success: true) hardcoded, so success_rate() was always 1.0
findings.current_state: record_tool_outcome passes the real tool_ok boolean into ActionHistory::record, so success_rate() reflects measured outcomes.
findings.required_invariant: Planner history records the actual tool outcome; success rates use real values (INV-PLAN-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR I): record actual tool outcome in planner history (fixes HIGH-009)

findings.residual_risk: Downstream strategy selection consumes this signal; its weighting is tracked separately under MED-009.

findings.title: TLS Configuration Is Not Integrated into the Gateway Serving Path
original_reachable_path: soul_gateway::serve -> TcpListener::bind + axum::serve (plaintext); TlsConfig had no call site
findings.current_state: serve_with_tls accepts an Option<TlsConfig> and, when present, serves through axum_server::bind_rustls; TlsConfig::load builds a RustlsConfig from a PEM certificate/key pair. serve() delegates to serve_with_tls, so TlsConfig is now on the live serving path rather than dead code.
findings.required_invariant: Binding a non-loopback address requires an active TLS serving path (INV-NET-2).

fixing_prs.title: Integrate platforms, automations, and secure remote runtime

findings.residual_risk: TLS is opt-in per invocation: serve() without a TlsConfig still serves plaintext. mTLS client-certificate verification is not implemented, and other listeners (ws_bridge, src/api.rs) have no TLS and rely on loopback binding.

findings.title: soul_llm makes a single HTTP attempt with no retry/backoff on transient LLM provider failures
original_reachable_path: run_react -> guarded_llm_chat -> LlmClient -> single provider HTTP attempt; any transient failure aborts the turn
findings.current_state: A RateLimited { retry_after } error variant exists in soul_llm/src/error.rs, but nothing acts on it. There is no retry loop, no exponential backoff, no jitter and no Retry-After honouring anywhere in soul_llm/src/client.rs or the three provider implementations. The only tokio::time::sleep in client.rs is inside a #[cfg(test)] mock provider used to measure concurrency, not production code.
reachable_from: soul-agent-core run_react -> guarded_llm_chat -> LlmClient::generate_with_goal -> provider generate (single attempt)
findings.reproducer: Inspect soul_llm/src/client.rs and soul_llm/src/providers/*.rs for a retry construct: the only sleep is within the test module. A provider returning 429 or a transient 5xx surfaces directly to the caller and ends the agent turn.
findings.required_invariant: Transient provider failures are retried with bounded exponential backoff and jitter, honouring Retry-After.
findings.residual_risk: A single transient upstream failure or rate-limit response aborts an autonomous run; combined with the absent circuit-breaker partitioning this makes provider degradation user-visible and non-self-healing.
findings.follow_up: Implement bounded retry with exponential backoff + jitter and Retry-After support in LlmClient, with tests using a failure-injecting mock provider.

findings.title: soul_llm has token-budget accounting but no request-level rate limiting or concurrency cap
original_reachable_path: LlmClient dispatched unbounded concurrent provider requests; token budget accounting did not bound in-flight count
findings.current_state: LlmClient holds an Option<Arc<Semaphore>> sized from LlmConfig::max_concurrent_requests (default 8, 0 disables). A permit is acquired on every dispatch entry point, and streaming responses are wrapped in PermitGuardedStream so the permit lives for the whole stream rather than being released when the dispatching future returns.
findings.required_invariant: soul_llm bounds the number of outbound provider requests in flight, independent of token-budget accounting (INV-PROVIDER-1).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR M): request-level concurrency cap for soul_llm (fixes MED-002)

findings.residual_risk: The cap is per-LlmClient instance and per-process; several clients, or several processes, can each open up to the cap. Per-provider request-rate limiting (as opposed to concurrency) is not implemented.

findings.title: Circuit Breaker with_service_name Is a No-Op
findings.current_state: Re-confirmed on current main: with_service_name stores the service name and it is used in state keying and reporting; the original claim that it was a no-op was factually incorrect.
findings.required_invariant: Circuit breaker state is partitioned by service where the API implies it.
findings.residual_risk: Partitioning exists at the circuit-breaker layer, but soul_llm does not route provider calls through it, so per-provider isolation is not achieved end to end (tracked with MED-001).

findings.title: ToT node evaluation uses hardcoded placeholder embeddings, making scoring and pruning non-functional
original_reachable_path: run_react Tree-of-Thoughts branch -> evaluate_node with placeholder embeddings -> meaningless pruning
findings.current_state: The sole production caller of evaluate_node, in soul-agent-core/src/lib.rs, constructs both vectors as all-ones placeholders (vec![1.0_f32; 64] for query and thought alike) with in-code comments reading 'placeholder' and 'using embeddings if available, else fake'. Cosine similarity between two identical all-ones vectors is 1.0 for every node, so every thought scores identically and pruning cannot discriminate. The genuinely varied vectors in soullink-reasoning/src/tree.rs are inside #[test] functions only.
reachable_from: soul-agent-core run_react -> Tree-of-Thoughts strategy branch -> ThoughtTree::evaluate_node(leaf, [1.0;64], [1.0;64])
findings.reproducer: Read the ToT branch in soul-agent-core/src/lib.rs: query_emb and thought_emb are both vec![1.0_f32; 64]. Their cosine similarity is identically 1.0, so evaluate_node returns the same score for every leaf and NodeStatus::Pruned is never selected on merit.
findings.required_invariant: Reasoning-quality scores that drive pruning must be computed from real semantic embeddings, or the feature must not claim to prune on merit (INV-TRUTH-1).
findings.residual_risk: Tree-of-Thoughts advertises semantic search but performs none; branch selection is effectively arbitrary while appearing principled, which can mislead operators and any evaluation built on it.
findings.follow_up: Wire real embeddings (soullink-eval or the configured embedding provider) into the ToT branch, or gate the strategy off and stop reporting semantic scores.

findings.title: DPO Training Collects No Negative Samples (rejected always empty)
original_reachable_path: DPO export produced pairs whose `rejected` field was always empty, making preference training degenerate
findings.current_state: The original claim - that `rejected` is always empty - is factually incorrect and was already incorrect when the audit was written. export_dpo_pairs groups trajectories by prompt, sorts by quality_score, pairs the best with the worst, and skips the group unless chosen.quality_score is strictly greater than rejected.quality_score, so an exported pair always carries a real, lower-scored negative sample. git log -S on the pairing expression dates it to commit d906d34533001ef7e7807e04abdf065600aab5a0 (2026-06-15), which git merge-base confirms is an ancestor of the audit baseline 5e3b0c3b0d18f6d0022c1c762821d9aad340b011 - so the behaviour predates the audit rather than being fixed by it. Classified FALSE_POSITIVE rather than FIXED_AND_VERIFIED for that reason.
findings.required_invariant: DPO export produces pairs containing a genuine negative sample.
findings.residual_risk: test_dpo_export proves chosen_score > rejected_score for an exported pair. Quality scores come from the heuristic critique path, so pair quality is only as good as that heuristic.

findings.title: Post-execution error and reward learning signals are hardcoded constants
original_reachable_path: run_react post-execution -> update_global_error/calculate_reward with hardcoded constants, so learning signals were independent of outcome
findings.current_state: Both functions now derive every component from measured state: prediction error from the turn/max_turns ratio, action error from repair_count/tool_call_count, goal error from GoalError::calculate word overlap, uncertainty from UncertaintyMetric::calculate entropy, initiative error from consecutive_failures/max_consecutive_failures, and reward quality from soul_critique::quick_critique rather than a fixed 0.8.
findings.required_invariant: Post-execution error and reward signals are derived from real measured outcomes (INV-PLAN-4).

fixing_prs.title: security(PR O): derive learning signals from real outcomes

findings.residual_risk: The underlying similarity/critique functions are heuristic (word-overlap and rule-based), so the signals are real and outcome-dependent but not semantically precise.

findings.title: soul-mcp WebSocket MCP server dispatches tools/call with no authentication
findings.current_state: serve_ws accepts every WebSocket connection with no authentication, no origin check and no token, and dispatches tools/call from it - the defect is real in the source. It is not reachable: a workspace-wide search for callers of serve_ws outside soul-mcp's own definition returns none (the same-named function in soul-protocol/src/lib.rs is a different type). No binary, including soulsystem and soul-kernel, starts an MCP server.
findings.unreachable_because: soul_mcp::McpTransport::serve_ws has no production call site in any workspace binary; only the client side (WsTransport::connect_client) is used, from soul_tools' mcp_call tool.
findings.required_invariant: An MCP server exposing tools/call must authenticate its peers before dispatch.
findings.residual_risk: High if it ever becomes reachable: the first caller to start an MCP server exposes unauthenticated tool dispatch. The code carries no guard, comment or feature gate warning of this.
findings.follow_up: Feature-gate serve_ws as experimental or add mandatory peer authentication before any caller is introduced.

findings.title: soul-protocol UDP Discovery Broadcasts Metadata
findings.current_state: The UDP broadcast discovery server still exists and would advertise node metadata on the local network, but no workspace binary starts it.
findings.unreachable_because: No production call site starts the discovery server; it is library surface only.
findings.required_invariant: Discovery must not broadcast identifying metadata unless explicitly enabled and scoped.
findings.residual_risk: If enabled later, node metadata is broadcast unauthenticated to the local segment.

findings.title: Inconsistent Retry Policy: fabricated tool success rates + strategy-less auto_repair
original_reachable_path: strategy selection consumed a fabricated success rate (always 1.0) and auto_retry had no strategy-level policy
findings.current_state: The fabricated-success-rate half is fixed by PR #80: success_rate() is computed from really-recorded outcomes and strategy_selector.record_outcome receives a real StrategyOutcome. The retry-policy half is unchanged: there is still no single coherent retry policy - soul_llm performs no provider retry at all (MED-001), while the agent loop retries at the strategy level, so retry behaviour differs by layer with no shared budget or backoff.
findings.remaining_exposure: Retries are uncoordinated across layers: a failing provider produces immediate strategy-level replanning rather than a bounded backoff, and no layer honours Retry-After.
findings.required_invariant: Retry policy is coherent across layers and driven by real outcome data.

fixing_prs.title: security(PR I): record actual tool outcome in planner history (fixes HIGH-009)

findings.residual_risk: Outcome data is now truthful, so decisions are at least based on real signals; the coordination gap remains a resilience rather than a correctness problem.
findings.follow_up: Define one retry/backoff policy shared by the provider layer and the agent loop; land it with MED-001.

findings.title: soul-wasm WASI host functions (fd_write/proc_exit/environ_*) are placeholders
findings.current_state: The WASI host functions remain stubs: fd_write ignores the iovs pointer entirely and returns success, and environ_* return empty. soul_wasm is a dependency of the soulsystem binary, but no production code path invokes the plugin execution API, so no plugin can currently be run through these stubs.
findings.unreachable_because: No production caller invokes soul_wasm's plugin execution entry point; the crate is linked but its execution API is unused.
findings.required_invariant: WASM plugin host functions must implement real I/O or the execution API must be gated as experimental (INV-TRUTH-1).
findings.residual_risk: If wired later, plugins silently no-op all I/O while reporting success, and fd_write's unbounded handling of an unvalidated iovs pointer would need bounds checking against linear memory before use.
findings.follow_up: Gate the execution API behind an experimental feature flag until the host functions are implemented and bounds-checked.

findings.title: Workspace build config globally silences dead_code, unused_imports, unused_variables, and deprecated lints
findings.current_state: Unchanged and intentional. .cargo/config.toml still passes -A dead_code and -A unused_imports, and the workspace lints table silences additional lints. CI's RUSTFLAGS repeats the same allows so the suppression is consistent between local and CI builds. CLAUDE.md documents this as an established repository convention.
findings.decision_required: Repository owners must decide whether to reverse the workspace-wide lint suppression. Reversing it under CI's -D warnings would convert an unknown and potentially very large number of currently-masked warnings across 184 workspace packages into hard build failures, so it needs an owner, a triage budget and a staging plan rather than an incidental change.
findings.required_invariant: The workspace build configuration does not globally downgrade dead_code, unused_imports, unused_variables and deprecated to allow.
findings.residual_risk: Genuinely dead or deprecated code, including orphaned security components (see HIGH-002), can accumulate without any build-time signal.
findings.follow_up: Owner decision, then a staged un-suppression: enable one lint at a time at warn level, triage, then promote to deny.

findings.title: Version inconsistency: root package 0.6.0 vs workspace.package 13.5.0
original_reachable_path: GET /health -> HealthResponse.version = env!(CARGO_PKG_VERSION) = 0.6.0 while all member crates report 13.5.0
findings.current_state: Unchanged. cargo metadata on current main reports the root soulsystem package at version 0.6.0 while [workspace.package].version is 13.5.0, so the binary's startup banner, /health response, metrics and backup metadata all report 0.6.0.
findings.reproducer: cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 reports version 0.6.0 for package soulsystem; grep [workspace.package] in Cargo.toml shows 13.5.0.
findings.required_invariant: The root binary package version and [workspace.package].version are identical, so every runtime surface reports one consistent version.
findings.residual_risk: Observability and incident-response drift only; no security impact. Misleading when correlating a deployed binary with a source revision.
findings.follow_up: Set the root package to version.workspace = true and add a CI manifest-consistency check.

findings.title: check.sh hardcoded a non-existent absolute repository path instead of deriving it
findings.current_state: check.sh now derives the repository root from its own location (cd "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)") instead of the previously hardcoded, wrong-case absolute path under /root.
findings.required_invariant: Developer/CI helper scripts must not hardcode a non-existent absolute path.

fixing_prs.title: PR P: repair cargo-deny config, correct MSRV, wire both as required CI gates

findings.residual_risk: The copy under the excluded os-agents/ tree still carries the original hardcoded absolute path; it is out of the workspace and not built by CI.

findings.title: scirust-gpu-macros #[gpu] is a non-functional placeholder, but unreachable
findings.current_state: The #[gpu] attribute macro still re-emits the original function body with no GPU dispatch. It is applied to no function in the workspace, and the main workspace neither includes the crate as a member dependency of a reachable target nor re-exports the macro.
findings.unreachable_because: No workspace code applies #[gpu]; the macro has no expansion site.
findings.required_invariant: #[gpu] must expand to a genuine GPU dispatch with documented CPU fallback, or be gated experimental (INV-TRUTH-2).
findings.residual_risk: A future author applying #[gpu] would get silent CPU execution presented as GPU acceleration.

findings.title: GPU Backends (Cuda/Rocm/Vulkan) Delegate All Compute to CpuFallback
findings.current_state: CudaBackend, RocmBackend and VulkanBackend still forward every compute method to CpuFallback while is_available() does real device probing (nvidia-smi/rocm-smi/vulkaninfo). get_backend() has no caller outside the module's own #[cfg(test)] block, so no runtime path receives CPU results believing them to be GPU-accelerated.
findings.unreachable_because: get_backend() and the ComputeBackend compute methods have no non-test callers in the workspace.
findings.required_invariant: A backend reporting a GPU device present must execute on it or be documented and gated as a CPU-delegating placeholder (INV-TRUTH-2).
findings.residual_risk: The device-probing commands (nvidia-smi, rocm-smi, vulkaninfo) are themselves bare std::process::Command invocations in the soulsystem binary; they are currently unreachable but are part of the CRIT-001 inventory.

findings.title: soul_planner CognitiveLoop uses keyword matching, not LLM reasoning
original_reachable_path: src/main.rs --plan flag -> CognitiveLoop::create_plan(&goal, &[]) -> empty plan, no LLM decomposition
findings.current_state: Unchanged. CognitiveLoop::decide still branches on substring matching over the context string, and create_plan mechanically maps caller-supplied commands to steps, so --plan with no supplied commands yields an empty plan. soul_planner still declares no LLM dependency. The orphaned src/autonomous_loop.rs, which contained a second keyword-decide cycle, is confirmed dead: no `mod autonomous_loop` declaration exists in src/lib.rs or src/main.rs, so it is not compiled - which also means the 0.0.0.0 listener bind inside it is unreachable.
reachable_from: src/main.rs --plan flag -> soul_planner::CognitiveLoop::create_plan (reachable, produces an empty plan)
findings.reproducer: Run the binary with --plan '<multi-goal task>' and observe a Plan whose steps array is empty, because create_plan is called with an empty command slice and performs no LLM decomposition.
findings.required_invariant: Reachable plan generation and action decisions derive from the configured LLM or an explicitly documented deterministic strategy, not substring matching (INV-PLAN-5).
findings.residual_risk: The reachable damage is limited: run_react does its reasoning through the LLM and uses CognitiveLoop only for memory/history, so the keyword path is not load-bearing for the main agent loop. The --plan CLI surface still presents an empty plan as a result.
findings.follow_up: Either wire --plan to LLM-backed decomposition or remove/experimental-gate the flag; delete the dead src/autonomous_loop.rs.

findings.title: Two integration test crates (both named soul_integration_tests) contain a Cargo.toml but zero test source files
findings.current_state: Unchanged. git ls-files integration_tests/ returns exactly one tracked file, integration_tests/Cargo.toml, with no src/ and no tests/. The manifest declares itself 'Integration tests for SoulSystem multi-crate workflows' but has no buildable target and is not a workspace member, so cargo test --workspace never runs it. A second copy exists under the excluded os-agents/ tree.
reachable_from: none - not a workspace member and contains no compiled code
findings.reproducer: git ls-files integration_tests/ returns only Cargo.toml. cargo build inside that directory fails with 'no targets specified in the manifest'.
findings.required_invariant: A package that advertises itself as an integration-test crate contains at least one test target exercised by CI.
findings.residual_risk: No executable risk; the harm is false confidence that multi-crate integration coverage exists. Notably there is still no end-to-end integration test proving backup/restore (INV-PERSIST-2) or a full agent run.
findings.follow_up: Delete integration_tests/Cargo.toml, or populate the crate with real tests and add it to the workspace members.

findings.title: soul_llm OpenAI/Anthropic providers lack native tool calling; chat() silently flattens tools to text
original_reachable_path: agent tool loop -> chat() with tools -> OpenAI/Anthropic providers flatten tool definitions into prompt text
findings.current_state: Unchanged. Only the Ollama provider implements native tool calling; the OpenAI and Anthropic providers do not send a tools/functions field, so tool definitions are flattened into prompt text and tool selection depends on the model following textual instructions.
reachable_from: soul-agent-core run_react -> guarded_llm_chat -> LlmClient::chat -> OpenAI/Anthropic provider
findings.reproducer: Read soul_llm/src/providers/openai.rs and anthropic.rs: neither request builder emits a tools/functions array, so tool schemas reach the model only as prose.
findings.required_invariant: Providers advertising tool support use the provider's native tool-calling API, or the limitation is surfaced to the caller.
findings.residual_risk: Tool-call parsing for these providers is text-based, so malformed or hallucinated tool invocations are more likely. Fail-closed dispatch (CRIT-002) means a hallucinated tool name cannot execute, which bounds the impact to reliability rather than security.
findings.follow_up: Implement native tool calling for the OpenAI and Anthropic providers.
